member.name: T:Milvonion.Infrastructure.Services.SecurityStampStore
member.summary:
Redis-backed revocation stamp store with the database (User.SessionStamp) as the durable source of truth. Reads are served from Redis for a cheap per-request check; on a cache miss (or any Redis failure) it falls back to the database and repopulates the cache, so a Redis outage degrades to one extra database round trip rather than breaking authentication.
A rotation writes the new stamp through to Redis and must run after the caller's transaction has committed. The read-through repopulation only adds a missing entry (SET NX), so a reader that loaded the old stamp from the database just before a rotation can never put it back over the new one.
While Redis is disconnected the cache is skipped altogether: a command sent to a reconnecting multiplexer waits in its backlog until the timeout, which would hold every authenticated request for seconds.

member.name: T:Milvonion.Infrastructure.Services.TransactionRunner
member.summary:
Default . The on makes the transaction interceptor open a transaction on the scoped MilvonionDbContext before the delegate runs and commit it afterwards (rolling back on exception). It is the same scoped context the repositories resolve, so the writes inside the delegate enlist in that transaction.
Being resolved and called through the interface is what lets the proxy intercept the call. A handler cannot get the same effect from a local [Transaction] method: a same-instance call bypasses the proxy (self-invocation), so the interceptor would never run.
